A valid jump sequence from 0 to y is a finite sequence p_0, ..., p_n with n >= 0 such that p_0 = 0, p_n = y, for every i with 0 <= i < n either p_{i+1} = p_i + a or p_{i+1} = p_i - b, every p_i is nonnegative, every p_i with 1 <= i <= n is not equal to forbidden[j] for any j with 0 <= j < len(forbidden), and there is no i with 0 <= i < n-1 such that p_{i+1} = p_i - b and p_{i+2} = p_{i+1} - b. Then: if there exists a valid jump sequence from 0 to x, r >= 0, there is a valid jump sequence from 0 to x of length r, and every valid jump sequence from 0 to x has length at least r; if no valid jump sequence from 0 to x exists, r = -1.
